description: did:key resolution MUST reject a key whose multicodec prefix is neither 0xed01 (Ed25519, varint of code 0xed) nor 0x8024 (P-256, varint of code 0x1200) with key_resolution_failed (RFC-ACDP-0001 §5.11.1 step 3). The DID below decodes successfully from base58-btc but carries the secp256k1 multicodec prefix 0xe701 over the sig-003 test key bytes — a well-formed did:key for a curve ACDP does not support.

input.scenario: Publish (or consumer-side verification) where agent_id / signature.key_id carry a did:key with multicodec prefix 0xe701 (secp256k1)

expected.behavior: Step 3 of the pure resolution algorithm: after multibase decoding, the prefix bytes MUST be 0xed01 or 0x8024 (the unsigned-varint encodings of multicodec codes 0xed and 0x1200); 0xe701 MUST be rejected with key_resolution_failed (permanent — the producer must re-key, not retry). The registry MUST NOT fall back to treating the remaining bytes as a raw key, and MUST NOT report unsupported_algorithm (signature.algorithm may be perfectly supported; the identity encoding is what is invalid). NO alternative_error_code is offered here, deliberately, unlike dk-002 and dk-004. Not because this case is harder to detect — it is not: the multicodec prefix is stable in the base58-btc encoding, so ed25519 keys always render z6Mk… and this secp256k1 key renders z6Dt…, and a grammar carrying a curve allowlist rejects it having decoded nothing. The reason is what the fault is ABOUT. dk-004 and dk-002 cases 1-2 fault the encoding of the identifier; this faults the KEY MATERIAL the identifier encodes — as does dk-002 case 3 (z6Mk), which decodes cleanly and is likewise step-3, and likewise carries no alternative — an unsupported curve. The remedies differ, and the code is what tells the producer which: schema_violation says 'fix your request', key_resolution_failed says 'this key is unusable, re-key'. A registry MAY put a curve allowlist in its grammar, but the rejection is still a step-3 verdict (RFC-ACDP-0001 §5.11.1, 'Which failures are resolution failures'). Widening this fixture would also leave nothing in the suite verifying that an implementation can tell 0xe701 from 0xed01 at all.
